## What

Linux sends data through AXI DMA into a simple Verilog AXI-Stream module in the
fabric (a running checksum, for example) and gets it back. This is the skeleton
every later RTL milestone plugs into.

```
Linux buffer -> AXI DMA MM2S -> [ Verilog: checksum ] -> AXI DMA S2MM -> Linux buffer
```

## Done when

- [ ] A 1 GB round trip with checksums matching on both sides.
- [ ] Throughput measured and compared with the B1.2 budget.
- [ ] The Vivado block design is checked in as a Tcl script (`write_bd_tcl`),
      not a binary project, so it can be reviewed and rebuilt.
- [ ] The stream module has a cocotb bench under `rtl_tests/` and passes
      `rtl / Lint (verilator)` and `rtl / cocotb simulation`.

## Notes

- Take clock and reset from the PS in the block design. This replaces the old
  `I-02` clock/reset sequencer, which existed only because the ECP5 has no
  processor.
- Get backpressure (`tready`) right here. Every module that later sits in this
  slot copies the pattern.
- Use the Xilinx XPM CDC and FIFO macros where a crossing or FIFO is needed;
  they replace the hand-written library planned in `I-01`.
